record.paper_title: Imaging with LINC-NIRVANA, the Fizeau interferometer of the Large Binocular Telescope: state of the art and open problems
record.original_question: How can image reconstruction for LINC-NIRVANA, the Fizeau interferometer of the Large Binocular Telescope, be extended from a space-invariant point-spread-function model to a space-variant point-spread-function model? In this setting, multiple deconvolution combines several interferometric images of the same astronomical target; the point-spread function can change with baseline orientation, adaptive-optics correction, and position in the field of view. A self-contained solution should estimate point-spread-function variation across the field from available star images, partition the image into domains where each point-spread function can be treated as approximately space-invariant, correct boundary effects inside those domain reconstructions, and recombine the results into a mosaic.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a Fizeau-type optical interferometric imaging system consisting of two circular apertures of diameter D separated by a baseline of length B, mounted on a common alt-azimuth platform so that the baseline orientation with respect to the sky can take prescribed angles θ_1,…,θ_p. For each baseline orientation θ_k the instrument records, on a two-dimensional detector of N×N pixels, a noisy image

   g_k(x) = (H_k * f)(x) + n_k(x),    x ∈ Ω ⊂ ℝ^2,  k = 1,…,p,

of the same astronomical target with intensity distribution f(x) ≥ 0. The blurring is assumed to be linear, but the point-spread function (PSF) H_k(x, y) depends not only on the baseline orientation θ_k and on the residual adaptive-optics correction in the field, but also on the position x in the field of view, so that

   (H_k * f)(x) = ∫ H_k(x, y) f(y) dy,

i.e. H_k is space-variant. The system can produce simultaneous images of a finite set of natural reference stars located at positions {x_j} inside the field of view, from which samples H_k(x_j, ·) of the PSF are available.

Devise a multiple-image deconvolution procedure for estimating f from the data {g_k}_{k=1}^p which:

(i) from the star images {H_k(x_j, ·)}, builds a model of the spatial variation of each H_k(x, ·) across the field;

(ii) partitions the field of view Ω into a collection of overlapping subdomains Ω_1,…,Ω_M on each of which H_k can be approximated, with prescribed accuracy, by a space-invariant PSF H_k^{(m)};

(iii) on each subdomain Ω_m performs a multiple-image deconvolution of the restricted data, using a method (for instance a maximum-likelihood iteration for Poisson noise such as the Ooe–Richardson–Lucy or Scaled Gradient Projection scheme) that correctly handles the boundary effects produced by the truncation of the convolution to Ω_m;

(iv) recombines the local reconstructions {f̂_m}_{m=1}^M into a single mosaic estimate f̂ of f over Ω in a way that ensures continuity and consistency in the overlap regions.

Provide a fully specified algorithm together with the convergence and accuracy guarantees required for it to constitute a practical solution of the space-variant multiple-image reconstruction problem for such a Fizeau interferometer.
artifact.status_search_result: The space-invariant multiple-image deconvolution problem for LINC-NIRVANA has been treated by several works (Bertero–Boccacci and collaborators), including methods for combining images with different baseline orientations, accelerated multi-image Richardson–Lucy/Scaled Gradient Projection iterations, blind deconvolution variants, and explicit reduction of boundary effects. Extension to space-variant PSFs via field partitioning and mosaicking has been proposed and prototyped in simulations, but a fully validated, general-purpose algorithm with rigorous accuracy/convergence guarantees does not yet appear to be established in the literature, so the overall problem is best classified as partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Reduction of boundary effects in multiple image deconvolution
status_evidence.snippet: Addresses boundary effects arising in multiple image deconvolution for LBT/LINC-NIRVANA, a key sub-step of the proposed approach.
status_evidence.claim: The boundary-correction sub-problem inside subdomain reconstructions has been solved.

status_evidence.title: Deconvolution of multiple images with high dynamic range and an application to LBT LINC-NIRVANA
status_evidence.snippet: Multiple-image deconvolution methods for LINC-NIRVANA with high dynamic range targets.
status_evidence.claim: Space-invariant multiple-image deconvolution methods for LINC-NIRVANA are available.

status_evidence.title: A blind deconvolution method for ground based telescopes and Fizeau interferometers
status_evidence.snippet: Blind deconvolution methodology applicable to Fizeau interferometers including LINC-NIRVANA.
status_evidence.claim: PSF estimation aspects have been addressed by blind deconvolution work.

status_evidence.title: Multiple Image Deblurring with High Dynamic-Range Poisson Data
status_evidence.snippet: Recent treatment of multiple-image Poisson deblurring relevant to LINC-NIRVANA-type data.
status_evidence.claim: Algorithmic framework for multi-image Poisson deconvolution continues to be developed, but space-variant extensions remain an active area.
